dedupe_keys.name: united states flood database 698 507 flood records from seven sources 1900 to 2020 li et al 2021

description: The United States Flood Database merges seven widely used flood inventories into one table with a common format, giving what its authors call the longest and most complete record of flooding across the United States. It was built by Z. Li and co-authors and described in Earth System Science Data in 2021. Coverage: 698,507 flood records in the United States from 1900 to about 2020, drawn from the NOAA Storm Events Database, the Dartmouth Flood Observatory, CyberFlood, the Indian Flood Inventory, EM-DAT, mPing citizen reports and the Global Flood Monitor; fields give begin and end dates, duration, coordinates, country, state, location, area, fatalities, damage, severity, cause (heavy rain, snowmelt, dam break or release, ice jam, storm), source and description, with added descriptors of distance to rivers, contributing area, flood zone, slope, elevation and land cover. Format and access: versioned CSV files (GFD v0.1 to v0.45) and processing notes in a GitHub repository, and a v1.0 archive on Zenodo; free. Licence (read on 2026-09-29): CC-BY-4.0 (Zenodo record); code MIT. Caveats: records inherit the biases of their sources, including media-driven reporting and geocoding from text, the same event can appear from several sources, and updates stopped after 2020 (repository last changed March 2022). Simulation uses: validating hydrologic and hydraulic simulations and building flood event catalogues for hazard exposure and climate adaptation of US infrastructure. Related records: the NOAA Storm Events Database (data-noaa-storm-events-database) and EM-DAT (data-em-dat) are two of its sources.
